title: Five ways to make a work DAG read as tracks
brief: Make parallel work individually followable and easy to extend while allowing strands to split, merge into a new strand, and split again—without letting visual grouping replace dependency truth.
defaultWhy: Confluence Corridors is the provisional whole-graph default at 94.8/100: it delivers the track feeling Zach described without adding track entities or hard borders. Lineage Lens is a fragile co-leader at 93.6/100 and should be spliced in as the click-to-focus interaction.
decisionHinge: The recommendation hinges on global continuity versus large-graph focus. Moving 6 weight points from layout stability/editability to density/focus flips the 1.2-point lead from Confluence Corridors to Lineage Lens. The practical splice is a Corridors resting view with Lineage Lens on selection.
invariants: Every direction renders the same ten-feature fork → two joins → review → re-split fixture and the same statuses.
Dependency edges are the only causal truth; proximity, color, area, phase, or lane never creates an edge.
A multi-area feature appears once, and filters must retain compact cues for hidden prerequisites.
Paper-minimal styling, visible state words/symbols, and no production Vibe Tracks mutation in this exploration.
boundary: These are standalone visual prototypes in the current Vibe Tracks paper vocabulary. Variant switching, demo toggles, pruning, feedback, splice selection, and export are real. File loading, automatic layout, saved hints, graph edits, cycle handling, and integration into the production renderer remain unimplemented and are not claimed as verified.

requirements.name: Path continuity
requirements.why: The graph earns the Tracks name only if Zach can visually follow one parallel strand without repeatedly reconstructing it from arrow endpoints.
requirements.passCondition: A viewer can trace an upstream-to-downstream route across the shared fork/join fixture in one scan.

anchors.1: Routes repeatedly jump rows or disappear into crossings.
anchors.3: The route is traceable but needs deliberate edge-following.
anchors.5: Whitespace, routing, or focus makes the route perceptually continuous at a glance.

requirements.name: Truthful forks and joins
requirements.why: Tracks may split, merge, and reform; the view must not imply exclusive ownership or relationships absent from vibe-depends-on.
requirements.passCondition: Forks and joins are explicit junctions and the downstream strand can begin anew without semantic ambiguity.

anchors.1: Visual grouping invents or hides relationships.
anchors.3: Edges remain correct, but grouping makes a fork or join ambiguous.
anchors.5: Every split and merge is explicit, readable, and faithful to the DAG.

requirements.name: Low-authoring file-first fit
requirements.why: Agents and humans should be able to add notes immediately; layout cannot become a second database that must be maintained.
requirements.passCondition: Existing dependencies, areas, and statuses are sufficient; any later hint is sparse and optional.

anchors.1: Every feature needs manual exclusive grouping.
anchors.5: The view works automatically from current files and writes no inferred grouping back.

requirements.name: Stable and correctable
requirements.why: A readable mental map compounds only if filters, refreshes, and one new task do not cause unrelated work to jump around.
requirements.passCondition: The fixture stays stable through the demonstrated state change and supports a predictable correction path.

anchors.1: Small changes broadly reshuffle the graph or cannot be corrected.
anchors.3: Mostly stable with some layout churn or limited control.
anchors.5: Deterministic placement, local change, and optional view-local correction are all clear.

requirements.name: Density and focus
requirements.why: Whole-project graphs grow; the view needs a path from ten nodes toward dozens without becoming a wall of ribbons.
requirements.passCondition: The same concept can suppress distant context, collapse history, or focus a selected lineage without losing boundary cues.

anchors.1: The idea fails beyond the small fixture.
anchors.3: Works for a few dozen nodes with scrolling or filtering.
anchors.5: Progressive disclosure and stable focus are built into the mental model.

hardGates.name: Dependencies own causality
hardGates.why: No visual grouping may create, erase, or reinterpret a dependency edge.

hardGates.name: No required second schema
hardGates.why: The winning direction must work on today's Markdown notes without required track metadata or a layout database.

hardGates.name: Same truthful fixture
hardGates.why: All directions must preserve every shared fork, join, node, and status so content choice cannot masquerade as design quality.

variants.name: Confluence Corridors
variants.thesis: Keep a general layered DAG, but make maximal path segments between junctions read as soft, borderless corridors.
variants.bestWhen: You want the whole graph visible and the Tracks metaphor to emerge naturally from topology rather than stored membership.
variants.losesWhen: The visible horizon is so large or dense that any global graph needs aggressive focus and collapsing.

decisions.label: Ontology
decisions.value: A track is a renderer-derived corridor between fork/join junctions, never a durable entity.

decisions.label: Layout
decisions.value: Stable layered ranks, crossing reduction, continuity bias, and faint wide under-strokes behind normal edges.

decisions.label: Adding work
decisions.value: A new dependent branches locally; unrelated nodes retain their coordinates.

proof: The preview renders the shared split/merge/re-split topology as continuous whitespace corridors.
The Add parallel task toggle inserts one local branch without moving the existing graph.

fr1.evidence: Wide neutral under-strokes and aligned nodes make each branch perceptually continuous through the whole fixture.

fr2.evidence: Corridors visibly terminate and reform at the actual fork and join nodes; ordinary dependency edges remain on top.

fr3.evidence: The concept derives entirely from dependencies, with areas available only as a soft ordering bias.

fr4.evidence: The local-add demo preserves all existing positions; production stability still depends on an unimplemented deterministic layout pass.

fr5.evidence: Corridors can combine with collapse and selection, but the standalone preview does not prove a 50-node graph.

g1.evidence: Thin arrowed edges remain the explicit causal layer above every corridor.

g2.evidence: No track property or saved lane is needed; the added branch is derived from one new dependency.

g3.evidence: All ten shared nodes, statuses, forks, joins, and outgoing review branches are visible.

variants.preview:
Confluence CorridorsThe DAG stays primary; whitespace and faint ribbons make local strands followable.
The new branch fits locally; unrelated nodes keep their place.

variants.name: Area Metro
variants.thesis: Use existing multi-valued vibe-areas as named route lines that may overlap, diverge, and reconverge.
variants.bestWhen: The same semantic workstreams recur across many tasks and their names matter more than a quiet monochrome graph.
variants.losesWhen: Features span several areas, route color proliferates, or area affinity is weaker than the actual causal chain.

decisions.label: Ontology
decisions.value: Areas are durable non-exclusive facets; metro routes are their visual projection.

decisions.label: Join
decisions.value: Several route strokes may pass through one task without duplicating that task.

decisions.label: Interaction
decisions.value: Selecting a route dims other areas while retaining cross-route dependency edges.

proof: The preview draws model, renderer, and agent routes over the identical causal fixture.
The route-focus toggle isolates renderer while preserving all nodes and edges.

fr1.evidence: Colored routes are easy to follow, but multiple strokes through shared tasks compete with status and edge detail.

fr2.evidence: Overlapping routes preserve real joins, though route continuation after a join is partly a semantic-area judgment.

fr3.evidence: It reuses existing areas, but useful output depends on maintaining a reasonably consistent area vocabulary.

fr4.evidence: Area names offer stable anchors and the focus action is predictable; multi-area changes can reroute the visual map.

fr5.evidence: Route focus helps, but many areas or dense overlap eventually creates metro-map clutter.

g1.evidence: Arrowed dependency edges remain visible independently of the colored area routes.

g2.evidence: The route source is today's optional multi-valued vibe-areas, not a new required track field.

g3.evidence: The same ten nodes and exact causal joins remain present while route emphasis changes.

variants.preview:
Area MetroExisting multi-valued areas become named routes laid over the same edges.
Strong semantic labels, but multi-area work makes the map busier.

variants.name: Lineage Lens
variants.thesis: Keep the global graph general and turn a selected feature's ancestors and descendants into the temporary track.
variants.bestWhen: Zach usually thinks about one feature at a time and wants its complete causal neighborhood without losing spatial context.
variants.losesWhen: He needs to compare several unrelated parallel strands simultaneously without repeated selection.

decisions.label: Ontology
decisions.value: A track exists only for the current selection; no global workstream assignment is implied.

decisions.label: Interaction
decisions.value: Clicking a node darkens its lineage, dims unrelated work, and keeps every node anchored.

decisions.label: Scale
decisions.value: Distant completed ancestry can collapse into counted boundary stubs.

proof: The preview starts with the same complete DAG.
Follow Snapshot highlights only its causal lineage and dims the independent dispatcher/live-loop branch.

fr1.evidence: The selected lineage becomes a single high-contrast route while unrelated nodes visibly recede.

fr2.evidence: Highlight membership is computed from actual ancestors and descendants, so every fork and join stays causal.

fr3.evidence: Selection plus dependencies is sufficient; no grouping metadata exists to maintain.

fr4.evidence: Anchored positions are part of the proposal, but the preview does not demonstrate adding nodes or manual correction.

fr5.evidence: Progressive disclosure is the primary interaction, making it the strongest direction for large graphs.

g1.evidence: Only the true ancestor/descendant edges receive emphasis; no proximity-based relation is introduced.

g2.evidence: The focus set is computed at render time from the existing snapshot.

g3.evidence: The base state contains every shared node and the focus state dims rather than deletes off-lineage work.

variants.preview:
Lineage LensThe whole DAG rests quietly; selecting a node reveals one causal storyline.
Best companion mode when the full project is too large to read at once.

variants.name: Chaptered DAG
variants.thesis: Keep the graph fully general and improve readability with phases, junction geometry, bundling, and collapse—not tracks.
variants.bestWhen: The word track starts implying too much and topological stage is the most useful stable grouping.
variants.losesWhen: The central need is following several long-lived workstreams rather than seeing overall project progression.

decisions.label: Ontology
decisions.value: No track concept at all; the DAG is grouped only by derived topological chapter.

decisions.label: History
decisions.value: Completed prefixes collapse into counted capsules while outgoing edges stay explicit.

decisions.label: Layout
decisions.value: Crossing reduction and whitespace do the work that lane borders would otherwise do.

proof: The preview uses the identical DAG without adding routes or memberships.
The collapse toggle replaces the completed prefix with one counted capsule and preserves its outgoing dependencies.

fr1.evidence: Clean ranks and edges remain traceable, but no persistent visual corridor carries the eye through the graph.

fr2.evidence: Forks and joins are ordinary explicit graph junctions with no competing grouping semantics.

fr3.evidence: Every phase and capsule is derived from topology and status; the files need no new metadata.

fr4.evidence: Topological chapters are deterministic, and the demonstrated collapse changes density without moving downstream nodes.

fr5.evidence: Prefix collapse and phase focus scale better than a fully expanded DAG, though selected-lineage focus is still needed later.

g1.evidence: The view renders only actual dependencies and status-derived collapse.

g2.evidence: Ranks, phases, and completed capsules derive from current graph data.

g3.evidence: Expanded state contains the complete fixture; collapsed state explicitly counts the hidden nodes.

variants.preview:
Chaptered DAGDrop the track metaphor; use topological phases, junctions, and whitespace.
Most honest general view; continuity comes from routing rather than named tracks.

variants.name: Hard Swimlanes
variants.thesis: Persist one exclusive named lane per feature and route dependencies across those fixed rows.
variants.bestWhen: Rows represent genuinely exclusive owners or resources whose stable responsibility matters more than causal flow.
variants.losesWhen: Work is multi-area, branches merge, or the join itself belongs to several conceptual threads—as in this product.

decisions.label: Ontology
decisions.value: Lane membership is durable and exclusive, so every feature must choose exactly one row.

decisions.label: Join
decisions.value: A merge node is assigned to one lane even when several lanes causally produce it.

decisions.label: Interaction
decisions.value: Moving a join between lanes changes presentation but cannot resolve the semantic ambiguity.

proof: The preview forces all ten shared features into four explicit rows.
Moving Review from Renderer to Agent merely swaps which downstream edge crosses lanes, exposing the arbitrary choice.

fr1.evidence: Horizontal rows are easy to scan locally, but the causal route repeatedly crosses rows at every fork and merge.

fr2.evidence: Dependency edges remain present, yet placing the shared Review join in one exclusive lane falsely privileges one stream.

fr3.evidence: Every feature requires maintained exclusive lane membership, including intrinsically multi-area joins.

fr4.evidence: Manual lanes are positionally stable and correctable, but correction is continual semantic housekeeping.

fr5.evidence: Lane filtering is familiar, but cross-lane edges accumulate as the graph grows.

g1.evidence: Explicit dependency lines still carry causality; lane proximity itself is not interpreted as an edge.

g2.evidence: The direction requires a new persistent exclusive lane assignment for every feature, including ambiguous joins.

g3.evidence: Every shared node and dependency remains visible in both demonstrated lane placements.

variants.preview:
Hard SwimlanesEvery feature must occupy one persistent named row.
Stable ownership view, but splits and joins turn placement into false semantics.

checks: Same fork, joins, re-split, statuses, and visual fidelity
One meaningful state change in every prototype
Five weighted criteria frozen before scoring and summing to 100%
Every score carries evidence and confidence
Hard gates separate causal truth from layout judgment
Pick, shortlist, reject, feedback, splice, and Markdown export
Prototype evidence is explicitly separated from production verification
